contract.assumptions: No unrestricted Boolean cubic, SAT or generic circuit counter follows. The hard fixed F8 depth-two family permits higher nilpotent coefficients and shows why the degree qualification cannot simply be dropped. A chain ring with e>1 is not a field: erasing its nilradical can discard the phase carrying the hardness reduction. Even e=1 does not turn the repeated-pair cubic into every other field-decoder promise. Keep quotient height, full ordinary coefficients, signed moment weights, radial phase and0^0=1. The generic Lauder-Wan backend is a mathematical dependency, not an implemented/executed engine. Reference field scans default to24 bits; archived examples and callback replays do not demonstrate polynomial scaling or practical advantage.
contract.costs: All original input/ANF bytes, coefficient and center acquisition, exact algebra, matrix/bit arithmetic, reconstruction and O(n)-bit outputs are charged. The all-depth repeated-pair bounds are O(Ln^2+n^12)+softO(d^31) time and O(L+n^6)+softO(d^20) space. Seven nontrivial cubic point counts use at most eight field variables; the zeroth moment is a binary Gaussian. The fixed characteristic/degree/variable-count Lauder-Wan theorem supplies the31/20 exponents. The broader contact implementation costs (2^kappa+1_(e=1 mod3)2^d)poly(n+L), kappa<=b-1; it is not polynomial for arbitrary growing kappa. The distinct rank-three theorem gives O(Ln^2+n^8)+softO(d^19) time and O(L+n^4)+softO(d^12) space. Gate programs retain their original independent inputs and pay actual live ANF expansion; dead/internal wires are not free counting variables.
contract.obstruction: The generic Lauder-Wan engine remains to be implemented if an executed polynomial-in-d terminal is wanted. Do not replace acquisition with a supplied coordinate oracle, omit callback internal work, remove the degree/height gates, or infer a practical speed/priority claim.
contract.provides: From explicit cubic Boolean ANF, acquire the chain algebra A=F_(2^d)[t]/(t^e), module coordinates, affine center and ordinary phase. For the acquired repeated-pair residue with one common nonzero phase scalar, binary pair types, d>=3,3 not dividing d,r>=2,b=2r+1, any depth e and quotient-quadratic height3h<=e+1, exact signed/zero counting has bit time O(Ln^2+n^12)+softO(d^31) and space O(L+n^6)+softO(d^20), n=bde, using the published fixed-variable point-count algorithm. The separate rank-three branch has a broader ordinary ternary cubic promise. At d=3,e=2, arbitrary higher nilpotent cubic terms make the same J_r residue family #P-hard; this is outside the all-depth theorem's degree promise. The generic point-count engine is unimplemented in this distribution; executable reference terminals explicitly scan a bounded field.
contract.requires: Input is n original independent bits and exact degree<=3 Boolean ANF with full bit description length L. Neither ring, field degree/depth, quotient height, affine center, module basis, phase scalar nor useful pair chart is supplied: the compiler acquires them and verifies coefficient identities. For the all-depth unbounded-rank theorem the residue must fit the actual common-gamma repeated-pair form, with a_i,b_i in F2, arbitrary radial tau, d>=3 and3 not dividing d. The binary quadratic has unrestricted rank but is supported on the first h layers with3h<=e+1. Field-level eight-state Gaussian identities hold at every residue degree; that does not remove the raw acquisition/deep-lifting qualification. A general point-count callback must return exact F_(2^d) cardinalities of manufactured ordinary polynomials; an integer/range check alone does not establish its correctness.

\section{The computational statement}
The input is $n$ and an explicit Boolean algebraic normal form
$p(x)=\bigoplus_{|S|\le3}a_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i$.
We charge its full description length $L$: index-list encoding uses
$O(n+(M+1)\log(n+2))$ bits for $M$ monomials; executable bit masks use
$O(n(M+1))$ bits. The exact signed and zero counts are
\[
 Z(p)=\sum_{x\in\F_2^n}(-1)^{p(x)},\qquad N_0(p)=(2^n+Z(p))/2.
\]
The number $n$ counts original independent bits, not gate states.
Let $F=\F_{2^d}$, $A=F[t]/(t^e)$, and
$\lambda(a)=\Tr_{F/\F_2}([t^{e-1}]a)$.
The first statement has $n=3ed$; the unbounded-rank extension has $n=bed$.
\subsection{The complete rank-three acquired family}
Let $H\in A[X,Y,Z]$ be any ordinary homogeneous cubic whose coefficient
$\mu=[XYZ]H$ is a unit. Let $Q$ be an arbitrary binary quadratic function
of $A^3/(t^hA)^3$, where $3h\le e+1$. The input may be any invertible
binary affine change of coordinates of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:quotient-family}
 p(x)=\lambda(H(x+a))+Q(x\bmod t^h).
\end{equation}
Neither $A,d,e,h,H,Q,a$ nor a useful coordinate map is supplied.

\begin{theorem}[Acquired weighted critical-ray counter]\label{thm:quotient}
For $d\ge3$, the family \eqref{eq:quotient-family} has a deterministic
polynomial-time exact counter from raw Boolean ANF. Every accepted
representation is verified by coefficient identities. There is no residue
smoothness assumption, factorization promise, or bound on the rank of $Q$.
One conservative bit-time bound is
\[
 O(Ln^2+n^8)+\widetilde O(d^{19}),
\]
with space $O(L+n^4)+\widetilde O(d^{12})$; the tilde terms occur only at
a depth-one finite-field terminal. The original number of independent
bits is $n=3ed$. All integer reconstruction uses $O(n)$-bit numbers.
\end{theorem}
The finite-field terminal uses a published explicit point-counting
algorithm, not an assumed oracle (Section~\ref{sec:fieldterminal}).
The accompanying generic implementation of that terminal is deliberately
limited to explicit enumeration within a stated bit budget. It never
labels that enumeration polynomial. For $e\equiv0,2\pmod3$ the executed
compiler needs no such terminal at any residue degree.

The quotient can contain $3dh$ independent bits and its quadratic polar
rank can reach the largest even integer below or equal to $3dh$.
